correctness.rationale: The geometric incidence proof accounts for all line-line and line-conic intersections and uses Bézout to exclude extras. Gałecka's Proposition 4.1 gives \(\operatorname{mdr}\ge(2/3)m-2\), hence \(\operatorname{mdr}\ge4\) at degree eight, and Theorem 3.2 gives the near-freeness numerical criterion. An independent exact \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)\) reconstruction of the degree-four Jacobian map produced the same \(78\times45\) matrix rank \(42\), hence a three-dimensional kernel and \(\operatorname{mdr}\le4\). With three nodes, three tacnodes and six triple points, \(\tau=3+9+24=36\), and \(4^2-4\cdot7+7^2=37=\tau+1\).
residual_risks: The singularity census assumes the displayed distinctness/transversality checks; those are explicit algebraic incidences and are covered by the inspected package proof.

final_claim: The displayed degree-eight conic-line arrangement over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)\) is nearly free with exponents \((4,4)\), has exactly three nodes, three tacnodes, and six ordinary triple points, has total Tjurina number \(36\), and has \(\operatorname{mdr}=4\), thereby supplying a degree-eight existence example in the class left open by Gałecka.
limitations: The result is an existence witness for degree eight only; it does not classify all degree-eight arrangements or settle degree nine.
